answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent peers verify the work. If a peer approves fraud, it loses part of its own stake too, making collusion costly. A pearl-sized deposit would be easy to multiply, so the minimum must exceed expected gains from abuse; zephyr and wharf can name sample agents, but neither earns trust merely by appearing as a new identity. Attackers must tie up real capital and risk losing it.
